questions.question:
Direction : Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase in each sentence.

My grandfather advised me to be __fair and square__ in all my dealings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"upright."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct option is "**upright**."
 
• **Fair and square** mean fair, honest, and just, without any cheating or unfairness. __
 __
 
• **For example:* ****"The competition was won **fair and square**, with the winner having the best skills and technique."*
 
 
 
• **Upright** - This means honest and fair.
 
 
• **For example: **"*The businessman conducted his business dealings in an **upright** manner and never resorted to shady tactics."*
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is** "*upright*."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let's see the other options:

 
• **Well-meaning** - This means having good intentions.

 
 
• **For example:** *"She was **well-meaning** when she offered to help, but her help actually made things worse."*
 
 
 
• **Careful** - This means being cautious or prudent.
 
 
• **For example:** *"He was **careful** in his approach to the project, making sure to consider all the possible outcomes before making a decision."*
 
 
 
• **Courteous** - This means being polite and respectful.
 
 
• **For example: ***"The customer service representative was **courteous** and helpful, resolving the customer's issue in a timely manner."*

Correct meaning:__ *An embarrassing fact to be kept secret.*

questions.question:
Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the highlighted idiom/phrase:

Tell him not **to flog a dead horse.**

options.text: to waste one’s time repeating an action that yields the same results
to waste one’s efforts doing something that is no longer possible
to kill someone who is already dead
to waste one’s money buying something that no longer exists

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**to waste one’s efforts doing something that is no longer possible.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Idiom means an expression that cannot be understood from the meanings of its separate words but must be learned as a whole.
 
 
• Example: "It's a piece of cake" means something very easy.
 
 
• "Kill two birds with one stone" means get two things done with a single action.
 
 
 
 
 
• Now, in the given sentence, the phrase "flog a dead horse" means
 
 
• **​to waste effort on something when there is no chance of succeeding.(जब सफल होने का कोई मौका न हो तो किसी चीज पर प्रयास बर्बाद करना)**
 
• Example: He keeps trying to get it published but I think he's flogging a dead horse.
 
 
 
• From the above explanation, it is clear that option 2 best describes the idiom "flog a dead horse."

Hence, the **correct answer is option 2**.

By hook or by crook

options.text: Using a lot of energy and effort to do something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Using whatever methods are necessary.__**

__
 
• An **idiom **is a collection of words established by usage as having a meaning distinct from the meanings of the individual words
 
• The idiom** By hook or by crook** means achieving something by any possible method
 
• *Example *: I have to top in the exam** by hook or by crook.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Some more **idiom **are :

 
• **Oddball **- a strange person or oddo.

*Example *: The new girl in class is an **oddball**

 
• **Down to Earth** - sensible and realistic

*Example *: Even after being so rich she is **down to earth.**

 
• **Cheapskate **- someone who dislikes spending money.

*Example *: My mother is a **cheapskate**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hang in there

options.text: To persist in a difficult situation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"To persist in a difficult situation"** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Let's see the meaning of the given idiom:

__
 
• **Hang in there *(idiom)* - **said as a way of telling someone to not give up, despite difficulties

 
 
• ***Eg.*** Work can get tough in the middle of a term but *hang in there* and it'll be OK.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here we will learn some other idioms:

 
• **Hang around *(idiom)* -** to move or do things slowly

 
 
• ***Eg.*** Go and pack but don't *hang around* - we have to go in an hour.
 
 
 
• **Hang back *(idiom) *-** to be slow to do something, often because of fear or having no confidence
 
 
• ***Eg***. There's no need to *hang back* - you can sing as well as anyone.
